links.outcome: Errors in LLM oncology answers, including outdated knowledge from recent publications, and potential clinical harm
links.effect: Incorrect responses most commonly involved information retrieval errors, particularly with recent publications; 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%) would have medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm.
links.quote: Incorrect responses were most commonly associated with errors in information retrieval, particularly with recent publications, followed by erroneous reasoning and reading comprehension.

links.outcome: Exam-question accuracy versus clinical safety of LLM answers
links.effect: Best LLM scored 85.0% on exam questions, yet 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%) had medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm if acted upon.
links.quote: If acted upon in clinical practice, 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%; 95% CI, 59.7%-94.8%) would have a medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm.

screen.reason: The study is an empirical benchmark evaluating the performance, error types, and potential clinical harm of LLM answers to medical oncology examination questions without testing any deployment practices or safeguards.
